_comment: Benchmark sample cases for Verdex P1. Cases point to .txt documents in this folder and list queries run across three execution modes (M1 single-shot / M2 single-model multi-step / M3 multi-model Panel+Judge). The g-series and F-big/G-super docs are ASR transcripts (contain typos) — they double as a test of ASR cleaning. Drop more .txt files + entries here to extend the corpus.

queries.text: What is the core lesson about investment risk that this story teaches? Analyze from both the psychological and structural angles.
What is the core conflict between Grantham and his clients in this story? Summarize each side's position and who turned out to be right.
Why did the elderly billionaire go to the White House to protest? What does this reveal about his values beyond investing?
What is the 'AI bet' described here, and what are the risks if the bet fails? List the specific economic exposures mentioned.
What did GMO's 'Reinvest in Fear' letter say, and how precise was Grantham's market-timing call? Give the exact dates and numbers.
Describe the Forbes debate between Grantham and Blodget. Who predicted the crash, and how accurate was the prediction?
What was the verdict of the Manhattan debate on whether financial innovation is harmful? Summarize Grantham's argument.
What is Jim Chanos's view on the current AI-driven market? What evidence does he cite, and what is his famous catchphrase?
Analyze the anatomy of the 1999 internet bubble as described here: what drove it, who was blamed, and what were the warning signs ignored?
How did the 2008-2009 financial crisis unfold and recover according to this account? What were the key turning points and policy responses?
How does this text draw parallels between past bubbles and the 2026 AI boom? What structural similarities does it highlight?
Synthesize the overarching narrative across this entire series: what is the single most important lesson about markets and human behavior that ties all the episodes together?
